questions.question: During an experiment to find the energy in a food sample, 10 g of water increased in temperature by 5 °C. Which equation correctly calculates the energy transferred in Joules?
Which two measurements are required to calculate a person's Body Mass Index (BMI)?
options: Waist circumference and height
Body mass and age
Height and body mass
Height and resting heart rate

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'recovery time' after a period of exercise?
options: The total duration of the exercise session
The time it takes for the heart rate to return to its resting rate
The time it takes for breathing rate to double
The period of time needed to fall asleep after working out

questions.question: How does fitness level typically affect a person's recovery time after exercise?
options: Fitter individuals have a longer recovery time.
Fitness level has no effect on recovery time.
Fitter individuals do not experience a recovery phase.
Fitter individuals have a shorter recovery time.

questions.question: Why do breathing rate and heart rate increase during exercise?
options: Cells need more oxygen for cellular respiration.
The body needs to lose water through sweating.
To reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
To slow down the movement of blood to the muscles.

questions.question: What is the direct cause of a deficiency disease?
options: Consuming too much fat and sugar
An infection caused by harmful bacteria
Not consuming enough of a particular nutrient
Exercising too frequently without resting

questions.question: Which of the following health issues is directly linked to an increased risk from obesity?
options: Heart disease
Scurvy
Color blindness
Anemia

questions.question: Which two units are commonly used to compare the amount of energy provided by food?
options: Grams or milliliters
Kilojoules or calories
Degrees Celsius or Joules
Beats per minute or Watts

questions.question: What is the main role of food as a fuel in cellular respiration?
options: To directly cool down the body's internal temperature
To transport oxygen from the lungs to the muscles
To provide energy for life processes
To construct new bones and teeth

questions.question: Which of the following contains only recognized food groups?
options: Protein, glucose, calcium, water, oxygen, carbon dioxide
Carbohydrate, fat, iron, blood, tissues, organs, water
Vitamins, minerals, energy, exercise, saliva, hormones
Protein, carbohydrate, lipids/fats, water, minerals, vitamins and fibre

questions.question: Why do different people require different amounts of specific nutrients?
options: Their needs change at different times in their lives, depending on their lifestyle.
Nutrient requirements are determined solely by a person's height.
Everyone actually requires the exact same amount of nutrients regardless of age.
Nutrient needs only depend on the climate of the country they live in.

questions.question: How can the amount of energy provided by different foods be practically investigated and compared?
options: By dissolving the foods in cold water and measuring the volume
By burning the foods and measuring how much they heat water
By weighing the foods before and after leaving them in the sun
By mixing the foods with acid and observing the colour change

questions.question: When investigating how exercise affects heart rate, which of the following should be kept as control variables?
options: The person exercising and the length of time spent exercising
The type of shoes worn and the temperature of the room only
The heart rate of the person and the breathing rate of the person
The amount of exercise and the starting time of the experiment

questions.question: In an investigation where the amount of exercise is a categoric independent variable, where should it be plotted on a bar chart?
options: On the y-axis
In the title of the chart only
On the x-axis
On a separate legend next to the chart

questions.question: What can changes in normal body appearance, function, and behaviour indicate?
options: They are always signs of improved fitness
They indicate that a person is eating too much protein
They can be symptoms of ill health
They show that the body is undergoing cellular respiration
